tasks.commitBody:
The unknown-edition message served two states with one sentence, and the sentence was false in one of them. 'Edition unknown — the list may be incomplete' is true when the collective-wide edition read truncated; it is not true of a dangling pin under a complete read — the read finished, the list is whole, one reference points at something deleted or unreadable, and nothing the user waits for will resolve it. A message added to stop the app asserting what it cannot back was asserting what it cannot back, in the state where waiting helps nothing.

The research finding that shaped the fix: the editor feed structurally cannot produce the dangling state — its unknown gate reduces to the partial flag alone — so both editor render sites are monomorphically truncated and untouched. Only the reader's single render branch, where both row kinds land, conflated the two. The shared predicate now reports the distinction it already computed — 'truncated' or 'dangling' — through one new reason function wired identically to the existing boolean (which is now a shim over it, byte-identical, so the two can never diverge); the reader branch selects the message on it. The truncated state keeps the existing key and wording, which is exactly true there; the dangling state gets its own message in all four locales, claiming no incompleteness and implying no wait. Per the amendment's fence, the discriminator reports a distinction #329, #331 and #337 already make — no new state, no new reads, no change to when unknown fires.

Every spec that asserts the unknown wording now names which message it expects; the fixtures that drive the dangling shape — including #337's own program-row 'Ghost piece' case — assert the new key, and the agenda program-row suite gains the dangling case it lacked.

Closes #342

(*MVOX:Palestrina*)
